And we want them all!
Just when we thought that we couldn't have any more respect for Team Cherry, the dev goes and uses its platform to highlight even more adorable-looking indies coming out of Australia.
The Cherry Time! showcase promised "a bunch of exciting announcements," and these were not Hollow Knight-related (until the last one, of course), but instead focused on a handful of titles coming out under the studio's publishing arm.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com

articles.description:
The game's first free expansion.
We had our fingers crossed that Team Cherry might reveal the release date for Hollow Knight: Silksong's first DLC in its special presentation today, and what do you know, it did!
Sea of Sorrow will officially launch on Switch and Switch 2 on 11th December. This is a free expansion, so all those with the base game will be able to download and dive right in from this date.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea Of Sorrow DLC Finally Has A Release Date

articles.description:
Raised eye Browt.
We know that Pokémon Winds and Waves will launch on Switch 2 at some point in 2027, but that's it. The Pokémon Company is still keeping quiet about the upcoming Gen 10 entry, but an announced gap in the long-running anime has some people already narrowing the release window.
Earlier today, it was announced that the Pokémon anime would be taking a whopping nine-month gap between the finale of 'Winter Voyage' in December and a new series starring Liko and Roy, which kicks off in October 2027.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Pokémon Winds & Waves Release Date Speculation Rises From Gap In Anime Scheduling

articles.description:
Let's dive in.
Rare co-founder Tim Stamper has begun uploading new videos to his YouTube channel 'InTimsWorld', the first of which being a deep dive into the development of Conker's Bad Fur Day (thanks, Time Extension).
Released in 2001, mere months before the GameCube landed, Conker's Bad Fur Day is one of the most recognisable titles on the N64, garnering critical acclaim and controversy in equal measure thanks to its raunchy themes and platforming satire.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Rare Co-Founder Tim Stamper Unveils A Treasure Trove Of Conker Dev Material

articles.description:
Bowser's Fury.
Happy belated Thanksgiving to all of our friends across the pond! As you all wake up to tummies full of turkey, you'll be pleased to see that former Nintendo of America President Doug Bowser has wished everybody a good one, too. The only difference is, he did it with a grim AI-generated post.
Oh, brother. Bowser shared the image yesterday, showing him sitting behind a Thanksgiving spread with Bowser and Donkey Kong posing next to him.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Doug Bowser 'Apologises' To The "Haters" Of His Icky AI-Generated Thanksgiving Post

There are, however, still a few spicy Switch 2 hardware and game deals peppered in there. So here we'll collect the best US and UK offers we find, updated throughout the day.

articles.description:
Your companion to a huge adventure.
Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.
That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

The first title released on the eShop in 2017.
If you've ever bought one of Jupiter Corporation's Picross games on the Switch, you've helped the series reach a major milestone.
The Kyoto-based developer has this week announced its Picross series for Switch has now surpassed one million downloads. Since the launch of Picross S on the Switch in 2017, Jupiter has gone on to release more than 20 Picross titles (including all sorts of crossovers).
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Jupiter's Picross Series For Switch Has Officially Surpassed One Million Sales

articles.description:
It's one of the platform's biggest third-party supporters.
Square Enix has been one of the biggest third-party supporters of the Nintendo Switch 2, and it seems it's already paying off.
In the Japanese company's latest financial report, Square Enix president Takashi Kiryu has credited year-over-year net sales (¥11.6 billion to ¥35.6 billion) and operating income (¥8.0 billion to ¥13.0 billion) profits partly to its sales on Switch 2. Here's what he had to say:
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Square Enix Says Its Efforts Supporting Switch 2 Have Contributed To Its Strong Financial Results

articles.description:
Includes a fix for Anarchy Battle.
Last week, Nintendo released a major update for its team-based squid-shooter Splatoon 3, bumping the game up to Version 12.0.0.
It included changes to multiplayer, weapons adjustments, changes to Anarchy Battle, and even a change to the GameChat feature on Switch 2. Now, following this, Nintendo has released Version 12.0.1. The English patch notes aren't live just yet, but it is only a small update compared to the previous one.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Splatoon 3 Version 12.0.1 Update Out Now, Here Are The Patch Notes

articles.description:
Legends Retold is just the beginning.
Ubisoft is gearing up to launch Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 original. While many have questioned the decision to remake a game that arguably still looks and plays great to this day, the developers have been clear in their intention to use Retold as a launchpad for the future of the franchise.
Now, in a new interview with The Game Business, brand producer Loïc Gounon has expressed much broader ambitions for the character, perhaps bringing Rayman more in line with something like Sonic in terms of visibility.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Ubisoft Wants Rayman To Become A Huge, Transmedia Star

articles.description:
Give us a tune.
Just last week, Nintendo announced that the upcoming playable and electric ocarinas, launching in conjunction with Ocarina of Time, will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. We still don't have a firm release date for either of them over here in the EU (and no invites have been sent out just yet, as far as we can see), but the good folks over at Nintendo have sent us a lovely playable model, so we can get a close-up look at it all the same.
So, we thought it would be only right to show you lovely lot what's in the box — it's always good to see it from a bunch of different angles before you decide whether to pick one up for yourself, after all. Below, we've done exactly that.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Gallery: Get A Closer Look At Nintendo's Playable Ocarina Of Time

articles.description:
What a vision.
Accessory developer Gamesir doesn’t often make controllers with the Switch 1 and 2 in mind, instead focusing primarily on Xbox and PC. So when it announced the new Nova Vision, my Spider-Sense tingled.
The latest entry in the mid-range Nova line, the Vision adds two unique features: a colour LCD screen for quick and easy customisation, and Hall Effect analogue sticks with adjustable tension without the need for extra tools. At $54.99, this is a compelling controller as it is, but Gamesir has also included a charging stand to ensure you’re always good to go.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Review: Gamesir Nova Vision Controller For Switch 1 & 2 - Unique Features Elevate This Mid-Range Pad

articles.description:
Wilds, Withered Worlds, Wind Monsters.
It's time for North America's Nintendo Download Thanksgiving update and our Switch eShop round-up for November 26th.
Monster Hunter Wilds may not have been the best-received game in the series, but we're intrigued to see how it plays on Switch 2. Rayman Legends Retold looks fantastic, although from what we played in our preview, did it need retelling? We'll find out soon enough. Elsewhere, The Ascent, Station to Station and Hela all look worth investigating.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Here Are All The Games Coming To Switch eShop This Week (November 26)

articles.description:
Saria, not sorry.
The latest Japanese charts are in from Famitsu, and in perhaps the least surprising debut in recent memory, Grand Theft Auto VI is a hit.
Rockstar's code-in-a-box release had a staggering debut week in Japan, pulling in over 200,000 physical sales and kicking Ocarina of Time's comparatively measly ~35,000 into second. It's shy of the 537,000 Link's latest put up in its debut week, of course, but for a box with no disc in it, it's not bad going.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Japanese Charts: No Prizes For Guessing What Has Overtaken Zelda & Switch 2 This Week

articles.description:
The biggest physical launch since 2019.
All eyes have been on the launch of GTA 6 this month, with the game's so-called physical launch being a particularly interesting litmus test for the future of the industry.
It turns out that even without any discs, GTA 6 has proven to be a monumental success in terms of physical sales. This comes via Christopher Dring at The Game Business, who states that the game enjoyed the largest physical launch since 2019 in the UK, generating £32 million in revenue in just three days.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: GTA 6's Physical Launch Has Been An Astronomical Success, Despite No Discs

articles.description:
Finding the cutting edge of sword combat.
Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto. Big Walk? Big deal. It’s all noise designed to distract us from 2026’s real legacy: that it’s been one of the best years on record for video game swordfighting.
Onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat. Blood of Dawnwalker’s directional combat recreated a scintillating sense of strike-and-counterstrike rhythm rather than asking players to hide behind defensive blocks. Then Phantom Blade Zero swans in with cinematic style and a dazzling flurry of wuxia sword strikes and somersaults.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?

The company has promised to released a patch addressing the concerns, citing the long load times that primarily occur when travelling to surface areas. It's also identified an issue in which long loads occur if your network connection is unstable.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com

articles.description:
"Does the universe have it in for us?".
There were a good few indies set for launch in September last year that ended up being delayed to escape the blast radius of Hollow Knight: Silksong. Aeternum Game Studios' Metroidvania, Aeterna Lucis, was one such title, pushing its release date to 3rd December 2026 to ensure it was way out of the way of whatever Team Cherry was cooking up. Heh, well...
Yesterday, the Silksong dev announced an upcoming 'Cherry Time' special presentation, promising news and announcements from the studio, and an update on the hotly-anticipated Sea of Sorrow DLC. The showcase is tomorrow (27th November), so there's every chance that, in dodging the initial launch, Aeterna Lucis has wound up right in the way of the DLC (thanks, Steam Hype).
Read the full article on nintendolife.com

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Earlier this year, New Radical Games rocked up on the scene. A successor to Simpsons: Hit & Run and Prototype studio Radical Entertainment, with original Radical co-founder Ian Wilkinson as CEO, New Radical looked to be trying to trade on some of that pedigree. So, naturally, when Simpsons creator Matt Groening seemed to indicate during a panel that Hit & Run could be making some sort of return, remake speculation began churning. Sadly, whatever New Radical were working on, it looks like that game's been cancelled.
Read more
articles.title: Rumoured Simpsons: Hit & Run remake could be dead in the water, as New Radical Games devs suggest their unannounced game's been cancelled

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
In the grim darkness of the week before the release of Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, developers King Art and publishers Deep Silver have released a demo model painter. It's your chance to pre-emptively run a brush over units from the new strategy game's four major factions – Orks, Adeptus Mechanicus, Necrons and Space Marines. The Imperial Guard are in the game too, but mostly as a tutorial army. What a slap in the face for the Imperium's vanilla humans.
Deep Silver are calling it "the most powerful Painter in Dawn of War history", which doesn't seem all that dashing a boast given that Dawn of War 3 came out almost 10 years ago and today's PCs have a fair bit more RAM in them. You can opt for Basic Painter mode in order to quickly knock together livery for entire armies, or fire up the Advanced Painter and get stuck into the weeds of individual armour and body parts, with a choice of materials, patterns, decals and weathering. Here be trailer.
 Read more
articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 gets a model painter demo, so you can make a mess of your Orks, Necrons, Space Marines and AdMech before they even hit the battlefield

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Honest to goodness news for Hollow Knight: Silksong expansion Sea of Sorrow? That I didn’t invent in a dream? Scarcely believable, yet entirely true. The watery DLC is releasing on December 11th 2026, a scant two weeks from now, and as with original Hollow Knight's expansions it’ll be free to those who own the base game. There’s also a new trailer, showing some of the gunpowder-jumping and fishy boss-battling Hornet will get up to while exploring those sorrowful seas.
Read more
articles.title: Go fishing and fire Hornet out of a cannon in Silksong's December-bound Sea of Sorrow expansion, which Team Cherry say is "unlike anything we’ve done before"

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Glagstone's "1-bit" aesthetic is a homage to Macintosh games of the late 1980s, cut with elements of art deco, Expressionism and film noir, but it looks like that mainly because it began life on lo-fi indie handheld Playdate.
In transplanting this eerie, story-driven city-builder to Steam, developers Valerii Krasnoselskii and Evgenii Kirichenko have fleshed out the tasty throwback art and shored up connections between the game's management and story layers, while leaving the crux of the experience untouched: you are the newly appointed governor of a remote northern island, contested by rival nations. You have come here to harvest the island's rich mineral resources, and now, the island is trying to drive you nuts.
 Read more
articles.title: Keep the lighthouse on and the villagers obedient in Glagstone, an eerie island city-builder with Macintosh-style graphics

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Pick up your feet, mayflies! Fatshark's co-op rat-whacker Warhammer: Vermintide 2 is getting some new mod tools. It already has a public SDK and modding framework, you say? Ah, but the new mod tools are better. They are a public-facing incarnation of the very same digital spellcraft Fatshark use to create the official levels and characters.
Read more
articles.title: "A new era" for Vermintide 2 modding dawneth, as Fatshark release powerful new tools for custom levels, models and animations

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
How dare you accuse me of being a friendless loser! I have loads of friends! Their names are R2-D2 and Clippy and Arnold and Rosie the Maid. They all live in my rucksack, ready and waiting should I need somebody to dupe a security guard or fill the air around me with explosive chaff. All except Clippy, that is. He's too chonky to stuff in a bag, which can make for tricky mission extractions, but he compensates for that with his generous selection of *voice drops six octaves* FULLY LOADED AUTOCANNONS.


With friends like these, who needs human allies? It's time to play stealth tactics sim Cyber Knights: Flashpoint the way it was meant to be played: skulking in a hole while buzzing, clanking mechabastards cleanse the map of any and all defenders. Don't spare the lead, Rosie. You were not built to understand mercy.
 
Read more
articles.title: Drone Pilots have come to Cyber Knights: Flashpoint, the stealth tactics game's "most complex" class yet, alongside a pet system and the promise of "assassin cats"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
'Yay, GTA 6 is out on consoles and lots of people are playing it' is a fairly harmless thing to say. Unless you're, I dunno, a development platform mentioning that in a post celebrating the recent success of a PS5 emulator used for making unofficial PC ports of console games. You know, the sorts of unofficial PC ports vibecoders and proper coders having been scrambling to make of GTA 6 since its Xbox executable was allegedly leaked. The sorts of unofficial PC ports publishers like Rockstar tend to quickly move to have taken down.
Read more
articles.title: "Does changing where games run cross a legal line?" Microsoft-owned Github ask in now-deleted post celebrating GTA 6's effect on PC port-focused PS5 emulator

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Maths is not my strong suit, I make no secret of this, so when I come face to face with something like sudoku I will admit to recoiling in fear at having to confront this issue. Numbers don't make sense to me at the best of times, and now I have to figure out the specific placements of them whereby each number can only be used once per section, and each column and row have to all contain numbers one through nine? Terrifying! No, thanks, I'd much rather do the exact same thing but with, I don't know, skeletons and ghouls and the like. Which, conveniently, is more or less what Dungoku offers, a genre mashup of dungeon crawling and sudoku with a retro dark fantasy vibe.
 
Read more
articles.title: Dark fantasy and sudoku fuse together in unholy matrimony in Dungoku, a dungeon crawling twist on the classic puzzle game

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Pinball remains such an intoxicating game because it's one where you have to constantly be on your toes. As the tiny metal sphere bats about the place, it's down to you to hit it at just the right time so as to keep racking up points upon points. It's a game of skill as much as it is luck. It is also incredibly silly, which is why I'm so tickled by Appulse, a sci-fi pinball roguelite top-down shooter that launched today wherein your ball is actually the main defence system on your spaceship.
 
Read more
articles.title: Your mothership is a giant pinball machine and your ball is its defence system in Appulse, a top-down roguelite shooter that's out now

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I'm a simple person. I see an anthropomorphic rat man who opens up his trench coat that is filled with regular rats in the same manner as one would with counterfeit watches in a trailer for a video game, I add it to my wishlist. There really isn't much I need in life, but that certainly fulfills those needs. And it's exactly what HARK THE GHOUL is offering, an action-adventure, dungeon crawler RPG set in a weird and nasty Victorian gothic city with an emphasis on free exploration.
 
Read more
articles.title: HARK THE GHOUL is a Victorian gothic dungeon crawler RPG that features a trench-coat-wearing rat man who wants to sell you rats a la counterfeit watches

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November, even as the company's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.
According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives."
Speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.
 Read more
articles.title: "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
Yesterday I made a significant error in judgement. In writing an apology to our readers, I made a target of one of our writers and I won't be able to undo that. What I can try to do is apologise to that writer, who I'm addressing now.
Read more
articles.title: An apology from RPS

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Ubisoft, they of the recently revealed generative AI-focused game studio Motherbrain, have denied they're forcing new games being pitched by their developers to integrate use of genAI as a rule. The publishers' statement comes in the wake of a report claiming that Ubisoft devs with pitches that don't use genAI are required to explain in detail why they've decided it isn't suitable for the game being outlined.
Read more
articles.title: Ubisoft now require their devs to explain why they aren't using genAI in game pitches, claims report, though the Assassin's Creed publishers deny they're mandating it

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The Fable reboot is finally set to kick the release chicken (I'm not sure that's an established phrase anywhere in the world, but roll with it) early next year, following a not small amount of time in development and multiple delays. Despite that long time in the oven having made it necessary to look beyond just the series' classic entries for RPG inspiration, Playground Games' Fable general manager has said the team's "original vision" of what a Fable game needs to be hasn't changed.
Read more
articles.title: "Clearly not everything has gone well" during Fable's lengthy creation, says Playground boss, but the "original vision" remains intact despite taking cues from other RPGs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Nvidia may have finally released a proper cure for their last graphics driver, 621.24, reportedly writing unneccesarily vast amounts of data to some users' SSDs. A hotfix late last week seemed to have made things better, but not fixed everything. Here's hoping driver 621.40 has managed to totally rectify things.
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia release new graphics card driver, hopefully finally fixing that SSD-hammering unnecessary write bug the previous hotfix couldn't seem to sort

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
After waiting three years for Relic to expand Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, watching DLC after DLC focused on expanding the roster of units available in multiplayer matches, Operation Torch looks like a welcome addition. It's a new 15-mission campaign set in North Africa. following two US officers as they try to break the German Afrika Korps' hold on the region.
Having played through the whole thing, I really want to say it's been worth the wait. Unfortunately, it's not so straightforward as that.
Read more
articles.title: Company of Heroes 3: Operation Torch review - moments of barely held-together chaos squandered by mechanical scripting

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Much like a huge dust cloud gradually resolving into an army of skull-painted bikers, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld continues to take shape in the course of developer blog posts. The latest Parablog digs into what I think is one of the game's most interesting aspects – you don't control one single unified civ. Instead, you amass a motley tribe by befriending, conquering, or otherwise assimilating a range of individual wasteland bands.
 Read more
articles.title: Paradox grand strategy Afterworld has a wasteland band mechanic that sounds worryingly like a continent-sized game of The Sims

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
No! I am not the Ironclad, nor was meant to be; am an attendant lord, one that will do to bind a necro, Exhaust a scene or two, advise the Regent; no doubt, an easy tool, Defective, glad to be of use, Politic, Silent, and Impervious; full of high synergy, but a bit obtuse; at times, indeed, almost ridiculous— almost, at times, the Fool.
It has been a while since I played Slay the Spire 2. I return to find the forums full of grief concerning a recently introduced sixth character - a minstrel of sorts, dressed in carpets, who shoots arrows out of a harp.
 Read more
articles.title: In good news for certain Slay the Spire 2 bosses, Mega Crit's latest beta patch is "mostly Fool-centric", with an absolute rain of nerfs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
In today's instance of a sentence I never thought I'd write, English football commentator John Motson has followed in the footsteps of Darth Vader. In the latest instance of a game featuring a dead celebrity's voice reanimated with help from generative AI, EA Sports FC 27 will soon have Motson offering words about passes and shots that clank off the bar despite him having died in 2023.
Read more
articles.title: EA Sports FC 27 to resurrect John Motson with help from generative AI, because apparently football games need someone yelling about goals from beyond the grave

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Update, 26th Nov: Yesterday I posted a version of this article in which I, and other RPS staff, got a number of things badly, badly wrong. The purpose of this update is not to hide from the consequences but to limit the harm inflicted by a specific section of the original text, which has been replaced in the highlighted section below.
I'm both furious at myself and intensely sorry to everyone hurt by the original version. We've published a followup post here.
Read more
articles.title: Letter from the Editor(s) #21: That game everyone is and isn't playing, and how we report on AI

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
I’ve been playing GTA 6 on PS5.
To be fair, I’ve made no secret of my plans to do just that if you’ve read any of our recent roundups of what everyone’s playing over the weekend. I can understand why it might leave a sour taste in the mouth, but it is what it is. No corporate gun has been pointed at my head as a mandate to temporarily forsake my PC and play the big game of the moment is forced into my hands.
Read more
articles.title: Any official GTA 6 PC port’s ability to deliver a proper first person mode would be its biggest ace in the hole, so reckon I, a traitor

articles.author: Katie Scott
articles.description:
At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason.
Read more
articles.title: Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Exoprimal, Capcom's 2023 team shooter pitting exosuited fighters against T-rexes, is the latest game to be handed an expiration date. Its online services will cease as of late September 2027, rendering it unplayable, with the game set to be delisted from stores in March.
Read more
articles.title: Capcom dinosaur shooter Exoprimal's servers will go extinct next year, as shutdown meteor looms

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise. Diplomacy! The soul of any Total War game. They're going to build on the example of Total War: Three Kingdoms, which does allow for some gratifying backroom dealing, in fairness. During my first Thringdoms runthrough, I played Cao Cao, a ruler gifted with the ability to hypnotise people into liking him while hating each other. I spent many idle hours instigating proxy wars. Medieval 3 is apparently going to take all that to "new heights". It is going to make Han politicking seem as sophisticated as texting "get your filthy hands off my bae" to everybody you know on Valentine's Day.
 Read more
articles.title: "More than just war and peace": Total War: Medieval 3's diplomacy system will build on Three Kingdoms' backstabbing, with rulers who aren't just focused on you

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year. That rough start has it in need of a redemption arc, which the Rust devs are hoping will be powered by going free-to-play and making changes like the revamp of sandbox mode they've just rolled out.
Read more
articles.title: Delivering "a more modern Garry's Mod" is the goal of spiritual successor S&box's revamped sandbox mode, as classic GMod's workshop addon system returns

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
One of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands. Titled "Leonida", after the game's setting, the port is a recompilation – that is, a translation of the game's original code into code that'll run natively on different hardware, rather than being live translated by an emulator as you play. It's based on an incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build of the game, including the all-important executable file, which was leaked earlier in the week by crypto grifter Cyberleek.
 Read more
articles.title: AI-generated GTA 6 PC ports get nuked in alleged Rockstar takedown spree, as former Bungie dev hails "most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
There are many different kinds of smarts, and the kind of smarts I am are absolutely zero help when it comes to games like Astario, a spaceship and space station building factory sim reminiscent of Factorio that just launched into early access. I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.
 
Read more
articles.title: I'm not smart enough for the blocky, Factorio-esque spaceship and -station building sim Astario, but now that it's out in early access maybe you could be

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
There can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).
 
Read more
articles.title: Bitmap Brothers' iconic, robotic RTS game Z is unofficially back thanks to an open source, 3D remake

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a new update for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.
 
Read more
articles.title: Bare fist, megastructure climbing roguelike White Knuckle gets its penultimate region in The Core, a sterile, hostile reactor sector that you'll probably die in

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
For publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games? CD Projekt Red were subjected to such questioning in their latest earnings call, part of which was related to sales figures of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, that boring kind of thing. But CEO Michal Nowakowski did also respond to a comment about how GTA 6 may affect the development of The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.
 
Read more
articles.title: "That philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6": CD Projekt Red are staying the course on The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 after Rockstar's smash success

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Another day, another Steam update! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.
 
Read more
articles.title: Valve push on with their Steam improvements by revamping the Community Market home page and adding a watchlist to it so you're bookmarks will be a lot lighter

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now announced that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a new, still-unannounced game for around six years.
Read more
articles.title: Ex-Respawn studio Gravity Well announces "hibernation" following previous failure to secure funding and layoffs, but insists "we still believe in the IP and game we were building"

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
In a recent interview with Korean outlet Inven, CD Projekt Red's narrative director Philipp Weber and vice president of story Marcin Blacha shared some words on The Witcher 4, focusing on their awareness that not only will it inevitably be different from The Witcher 3, but also that it needs to be in order to justify its existence. Simultaneously, there's a certain something to The Witcher as a series that they feel is difficult to make tangible, but is something they want to ensure they don't lose sight of.
Read more
articles.title: "It would end up appealing to no one":  The Witcher 4 narrative leads aren't willing to strip away the series' "distinct edge" in the name of chasing a broader audience

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
GenAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI. More recently, one or more apparent crypto grifters claim to have naughtily tinkered with GTA VI, sparking attempts to  vibe-recomp an unoffical PC version. However, contrasting Zelnick's position is tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik, who quite confidently stated in an interview with Gamesindustry.biz that "devs shouldn't be afraid of it."
Read more
articles.title: "Game feel is impossible to copy": CEO of Probably Stolen publisher tinyBuild says devs "shouldn't be afraid" of AI clones

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Dancing Dragons Games and Hooded Horse have announced Symphony of War II: Dominion, the sequel to 2022's Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga.  Sin noted the original as pretty special for being "a good strategy game", highlighting the unique importance of taking care of each and every army member, rather than just benching the ones that are less effective and/or pretty to look at. The Nephilism Saga is also somewhat rare in being a turn-based tactics game made in RPG Maker, as seems to be the case with its sequel, which is expanding to include naval combat.
Read more
articles.title: Hooded Horse's latest tactics RPG is a sequel to Symphony of War, one of 2022's undersung favourites

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Despite being announced back in 2022 with an initial release window of 2025, NEKCOM's action RPG Showa American Story has been set for a late 2026 release date for a while now. That seems to have changed, however, as the release date on its Steam page has slipped to 2027 without any sort of announcement as to why.
Read more
articles.title: Action RPG Showa American Story seemingly delayed into 2027, with no comment on why from developer NEKCOM

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Following the full game list for Awesome Games Done Quick being released a little while ago, GDQ have now published the full schedule for the event running for a week from January 3rd through January 10th in Atlanta (and streamed on Twitch, of course). Included amongst the new games this year are 2026 releases like Queen's Domain, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the Ocarina of Time remake, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which all make a lot of sense as games practically made for speedrunning. Belmont's Curse, specifically, is set to be the event's final bonus game, only to be played if donation incentives are met (which I'm sure they will be, it's a Castlevania game at GDQ).
Read more
articles.title: GDQ releases schedule for Awesome Games Done Quick 2027 in January, featuring new runs like Queen's Domain, Big Walk, Galactic Racer, and the incongruously not-new Yakuza 5

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
GTA 6 leaker or leakers Cyberleek claim to to have released the main executable file for an alleged Xbox build of the game that they asserted they'd lobbed onto the net last week. In a fresh statement, the leakers alluded to the excutable being used in attempts to create an unofficial PC port of the crimsim, and denied that their use of cryptocurrency is just a grift.
Read more
articles.title: "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects": GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek claims to have released crimsim's Xbox executable and denies crypto grifting

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a new version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.
  
Read more
articles.title: 28 years later, grizzled XCOM-style WW2 tactics game Soldiers at War gets a fresh tour of duty on modern PCs

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Ho ho ho, the RPS Advent Calendar 2026 is... not ready yet. We haven’t written the words, and I keep forgetting to unblur that new picture of Horace (drawn by the reliably talented Amanda Flagg). But while drag our lumpen feet on the business of deciding our favourite games this year, RPS readers have begun plotting, and scheming, and apparently in some cases, spreadsheeting. That’s right: the Advent Calendar Guessing Game has returned, and is open right now for keen participants.
Read more
articles.title: Think you know games? That we liked? This year? Then join the RPS Advent Calendar Guessing Game 2026

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Literal decades ago, I tried to make a first-person RPG in HyperCard. I got as far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for the shareware version. I mention this because new, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.
This risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.
 Read more
articles.title: Might and Magic meets, er, paper in sunny new RPG Rise of Furax, a turn-based island tale that is entirely drawn by hand

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.
Read more
articles.title: "Don't let this happen again": GTA 6 hacker who pleaded guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach released under supervision

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's important questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.
 Read more
articles.title: Finally, some former Valorant and Sky devs have answered the call for a Peak-style platformer about throwing a cat through a hole in spacetime

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Fine Monday to ya, reader. In the interest of allowing Edwin more time to spend with his interview transcripts, you’ve got me on Maw duty this week. Not much chance of it going ungorged, in any case – while the continued bellows of Grand Theft Auto VI have frightened away most of the air-quotes "big" games from this late November habitat, many others remain, undaunted. Or because they probably thought the Venn diagram of GTA fans and grand strategy expansion fans was just two rings.
There’s still some Vice City-adjacent matters we’ll be covering this week – chief among them the Rockstar North unionisation vote, which is set to close in the coming days – but as I said to Edwin and Mark this morning, the cool thing about the continued lack of a PC version is that it leaves open a space to be filled with other things. Judging by what’s out this week, there’s certainly no shortage to choose from.
Read more
articles.title: This week in PC games: Raise a psychedelic baby, invent terrible new religions, and run your own PC hardware business

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Yep, he's back. Less than two weeks after Jensen Huang resigned from being CEO of Nvidia following reports of multiple affairs, the company's board have reinstated him "effective immediately".
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following alleged affairs, as US government support renders 'please give me my job back, go USA' a highly persuasive plea

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.


In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.
 
Read more
articles.title: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
An update for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently announced the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.
Read more
articles.title: Undisclosed AI-generated music pulled from The Binding of Isaac Repentance+ update, as attempt to get satirical on GTA 6 launch day goes awry

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Sundays are for googling local purveyors of live Christmas trees, the sole upside of no longer having a cat being that you can once again enjoy the smell of chopped woodland without the risk of it poisoning a family member. Well, then again, I mean... empirically speaking, you're probably just assuming that your human loved ones haven't eaten spruce needles. Can you say for an absolute fact that they wouldn't?
Fortunately, while your nan is off having her stomach pumped, you can pass the time by reading some good words from this week.
Read more
articles.title: The Sunday Papers

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.
 
Read more
articles.title: Alt Video is a digital, faux Blockbuster video store that you can fill with movies from your Letterboxd watchlist and Plex server

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own shows through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.
 
Read more
articles.title: Public-access television is born anew in NIGHT EYE TV, a digital goggle box filled with art game curios

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Oh I do love an eldritch horror creature, I do, especially one that at first glance may only be slightly different from what I'm used to seeing. Eldritch Empathy, then, seems like a grand ole game to satisfy my wanton need to experience such things. It's a puzzle roguelite that isn't exactly a Papers Please-like but certainly feels reminiscent of one, where you have to "analyse corrupted creatures, purify their emotions and learn how to communicate with an eldritch being."
 
Read more
articles.title: Eldritch Empathy is a Papers Please-esque roguelite about diagnosing cosmic horror creatures and trying not to lose your marbles as you do

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person. It was probably a wise choice on his part, obfuscating his current appearance with everyone's favourite annoying dog, essentially never speaking aloud in livestreams and instead using a text-to-speech bot, and posting only when there's notable enough Deltarune updates of if it would be very funny. But as it turns out, that sense of mystery extends to the team that's making Deltarune too, as Fox won't tell his devs how the game ends until they've built enough of it.
 
Read more
articles.title: "Everyone agrees it's more fun this way": Toby Fox won't tell his team how Deltarune ends until they've built enough of it

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel. No, in fact the next bit of DLC for Darkest Dungeon 2 was teased only a couple of weeks ago, with a new trailer shared today actually showing off what it's all about.
 
Read more
articles.title: Darkest Dungeon 2's next bit of DLC is a short run, combat focused gauntlet where you must do everything in your power to please the audience

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Terrible news, readers. Not only have several members of the Treehouse abandoned us, citing flimsy excuses like "James, you remember I've got that holiday booked, right?," many that remain have forsaken their duties and are playing something called a Play Station. What, all those Not GTA retrospectives we ran this week not inspiring enough for you? Can't even wait an indeterminate amount of time for a completely unconfirmed PC port? For what, some silly little cultural event of staggeringly vast and likely medium-altering importance? Whatever, was still made with union busting. Allegedly.
On the plus side, all the absences this week does mean the perfidy can be done and dusted quickly. Here's what we're playing this weekend:
Read more
articles.title: What are we all playing this weekend?

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia's latest graphics card driver appears to be unnecessarily writing to PC SSDs, something that's dumb, annoying and definitely warrants reverting

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.
However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.
We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.
Read more
articles.title: Vote now for 2026's RPS 100: Reader Edition

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.
Read more
articles.title: Akira Kurabayashi, company director at Arika and developer on Street Fighter EX, Tetris 99, Fighting EX Layer and more, has sadly passed away due to heart failure

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".
Read more
articles.title: Amid a year of layoffs, Ubisoft yank the cover off Motherbrain, their new studio "focused on AI for gameplay innovation"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Cyberleek, the GTA 6 leaker or leakers who shared a bunch of alleged gameplay earlier this year, are now claiming to have released a nearly complete in-development build of the crimsim's Xbox version. Continuing their established grift, the leaker or leakers are threatening to release the main executable file they've withheld unless people pump up the value of their cryptocurrency.
Read more
articles.title: GTA 6 leaker claims to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of Rockstar's crimsim onto the net, shouts that the "community will have it emulated inside a week"

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.
Read more
articles.title: Valve are pausing Steam Machine 2TB orders over "supply constraints," though the 512GB model is free of its waitlist

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.
Read more
articles.title: Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be important or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has launched on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere."
 
Read more
articles.title: Ignore that other game about crime that's out and burgle some ugly farmhouses in Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" with a 2000s Cartoon Network vibe

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada. Both studios affected, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, had a hand in last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows, with Montreal especially being a major and long-tenured development hub for the company.
Read more
articles.title: Ubisoft lay off 166 more staff, this time at their Montreal and Quebec City studios, while mumbling about "current production priorities and business needs"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Epic Games are, as you're probably aware, going big on genAI at the moment. To the extent that, last month, the Tim Sweeney-helmed company announced the Epic AI MegaJam. Build a playable game in Unreal Engine or Unreal Editor for Fortnite with help from as many AI agents or tools as you like was the pitch.
So, naturally, sorting the submissions by 'Popular' turns up a game about a fish with a sniper rifle whose creator says they deliberately made it without using any generative AI.
Read more
articles.title: Fish with a sniper rifle takes aim at Tim Sweeney's hopes and dreams, as genAI-free meme game tops Epic Games' vibe-coding megajam

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.
Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.
 Read more
articles.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world

articles.author: Jeremy Laird
articles.description:
Your next gaming monitor should be an OLED display. There, I've said it. And I know the notion won't please everyone. After all, a large grey proboscidean lumbers into the room whenever OLED technology is mentioned. Put simply, almost any risk of the dreaded burn-in is an immediate deal-breaker for some. I do get that.
Likewise, despite my musings just the other day on how affordable gaming monitors have generally become and the fact you can now snag an OLED panel, specifically, for sub £300 / $300, it's a stretch to say OLED gaming comes cheap. And yet here I am arguing firmly in favour of OLED.
Read more
articles.title: They're more complicated and more expensive than LCD screens, but your next gaming monitor should still be an OLED

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Try not to get whole armies of Space Marines pasted against the surfaces of planets thanks to your shoddy tactics, please. So ask the bosses of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, who're keen not to have their training workloads doubled because you're a crap general and have gotten a tight-knit force of uber-tough grunts killed unnecessarily, hope as they watch you play. This and other things have been emphasised by a fresh stream showing off over an hour of campaigning in the strategy warhammerer.
Read more
articles.title: Hour-long Total War: Warhammer 40,000 campaign stream shows off ship battle-less fleet management, makes clear how not ideal getting Space Marine armies killed is

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The employment tribunal over Rockstar's firing of 34 workers last year has come to an end for now, pending a final verdict from the judge. Said judge hasn't offered a concrete estimate of when her judgement will arrive, but has reportedly asserted that she'll provide it "as quickly as [she] possibly can".
Read more
articles.title: Rockstar firings tribunal hears closing statements, with judge promising to deliver a verdict "as quickly as I possibly can" - though it may take a while

articles.author: Max Moser
articles.description:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth, the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.
Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.
Read more
articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!


Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.
  
Read more
articles.title: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Funky feudal family frolic Crusader Kings 3 got its second major expansion of the year this week. It's called Silk and Silver (read my impressions), is all about merchant republics, and shipped alongside a beefy free update to the base game which - while largely focused on overhauling economics - also has some funny patch notes and features worth being aware of.
Read more
articles.title: "Abducting your own lover no longer gives you opinion of yourself" declare the notes for Crusader Kings 3's free Florin update, released alongside Silk and Silver

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.
A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.
You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.
Read more
articles.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.
In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."
 Read more
articles.title: "It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 launches on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
In a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.
Read more
articles.title: SteamDB will add "affiliate links to authorised game retailers" and a new tab dedicated to mods, first update since Nexus Mods takeover confirms

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.
 Read more
articles.title: Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.
The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.
Read more
articles.title: PC remains GTA 6's last hope for 60fps smoothness as Rockstar confirm such an option isn't coming to even the swankiest consoles

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.
 Read more
articles.title: Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.
Read more
articles.title: Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.
 
Read more
articles.title: Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.
 
Read more
articles.title: The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.
 
Read more
articles.title: Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!
 
Read more
articles.title: Archetype go all in on the Mass Effect vibes with a FemJun reveal, but I'm just left hoping they'll call the alternative option MascJun to balance it out

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.
It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.
 Read more
articles.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.
 
Read more
articles.title: Only two days out from GTA 6, its publisher Take-Two lay off staff at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.
Read more
articles.title: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Update 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:
The original article continues below.
As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.
Read more
articles.title: Embracer begin yet another round of layoffs at Crystal Dynamics, while they're still midway through development on two Tomb Raider games

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest update post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.
Read more
articles.title: Former Dishonored designer joins the team on New Blood's Victorian immersive sim Gloomwood, with a new level and new weapons coming this year

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
